utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Tuesday. I would like to greet the accused, Defence counsel, the witness, Mr. Scott and his associate, and all the people assisting us today. Registrar, I believe you have three IC numbers to give us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. 2D has submitted its objections to the list of documents tendered by the OTP via witness Ivan Bagaric. This list shall be given Exhibit IC994. 4D has also submitted their objections to the list of documents tendered by Witness Ivan Bagaric. This list shall be given Exhibit IC995. And the OTP has submitted its objections to the list of documents tendered by 2D and 3D via Witness Ivan Bagaric. This list shall be given Exhibit IC996. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Ms. Alaburic, I'll give you the floor back again. I believe you had a question which you wished to put to the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And a special good morning to you, Mr. Juric. We're going to start with a document today that we were discussing yesterday, and in my binder it is 2D774. Yes, 774. Have you found it, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to clarify what KOS is, to start off with. Was KOS the secret service of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, during the 1990s, was the secret service in the Army of Republika Srpska considered to be the KOS as well, or any other Serb army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, read this penultimate paragraph, and it says: "During negotiations with the commanders of the BH Army in Parsovici, the most extreme views were held by Jusa Hadzajlic, nicknamed Homeini, and we believe he encourages the conflict the most. It is not excluded that he is a KOS member," or a KOS man. Now, tell me, Mr. Juric, the members of the HVO, did they sometimes consider that extremists like this among the Muslim forces were, in fact, members of KOS and that they intentionally tried to fan the flames of conflict with the Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this gentleman here, but from unofficial talks, I heard that he lived and worked in Klis and that he cooperated closely with the commander of this brigade, the Neretvica Brigade, in Klis. As to the other details about his work and duties, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to the next document. It is 2D775, which is a document sent by Mr. Slavko Puljic on the 8th of April, 1993, to the Main Staff and the operations zone, informing them of the work of the commission. Tell me first, please, Mr. Juric, whether you knew that Slavko Puljic was a member of the commission of the BH Army and the HVO which was supposed to calm tensions in the area.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, in this report, mention is made of the attack on the barracks, called Goran Stanic in Seonica, and it goes on to say that the attack stopped. Now, does that correspond to what you knew about this period referred to in the report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at his conclusion together, where he says that, taking control of the barracks, the HVO forces would be routed and would influence their ability to defend, and that the Neretvica Brigade constantly asked for reinforcements from Prozor. Does that correspond to what you knew the situation to be on the ground, in the field?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what the commander of our brigade informed us about, it was precisely these elements that were discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, your answer has been recorded now. Let's go on to the next document, which is 2D776. Once again, we have Slavko Puljic writing on the following day, which is the 9th of April, 1993, and he says that the day was calm with further provocations. And in the middle of the text, he says that passersby going to Boksevica were still being harassed, and he quotes as an example the disarming of "one of our communications officers who was returning from Boksevica with a group of soldiers." Now, tell me whether this kind of provocation and incidents like this corresponds to what you knew about the situation at the beginning of April 1993 in the area.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document, which is P1874, and that is a collection of reports from the HVO Main Staff for the 13th of April. It's a collective report for the 13th of April. And if we look at page 2, under point 3, we have a heading there which says "Reports from Konjic." There are three of them, and we're going to comment on each of them briefly. In the first report, it says, "for the 13th of April." Now, tell me, please, the 13th of April, that's when the all-out attack by the BH Army started against HVO forces in the Konjic area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says here that on that day, the 13th of April, in the early-morning hours, the Croatian village of Buscak was attacked and then that attempts were made to cross the lake from Ostrozac and to take control of Falanovo Brdo and that Buturovic Polje was shelled with the 15 shells. Now, tell us, please, Mr. Juric, this description of events, does it correspond to what you know happened in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time on this particular day, I didn't know of operations of this kind, but I learnt about them later on, because between the 13th and 14th, that was the date when there was a clash in my area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I see, thank you. Now, as to report 2, the village of Buscak is mentioned once again, and it says that the village is about to fall. Tell us, did it indeed fall on that day and the following day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it did fall, but whether it was that day or the next day, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, it says that a strong reinforcement arrived from Jablanica, and that is reinforcement in the BH Army, and that they were moving towards Mrakovo and Zuglici, with the object of taking control of Boksevica. Tell us, Mr. Juric, to the best of your knowledge, regardless of the fact that this relates to another area in Konjic municipality, did the BH Army really attempt to take control of Boksevica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I wasn't in the area myself, but Boksevica was a dominant elevation from which you could control the whole area, so quite certainly in that operation it was part of the plan, and they probably wanted to take control of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Boksevica is the name of a large hill in the area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the highest elevation, the highest feature in the Klis area, from which you can control Jablanica and Prozor, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at the last sentence in report number 3, which says: "This is an all-out attack on the entire zone of Konjic and Jablanica." Would you agree with that? Is that what happened in the area at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now let's take a look at the next document, which is P1879. And once again that is a collective set of reports from the HVO for the 14th of April. And if we look at number 4, which is on page 2 of your document, Mr. Juric, once again we have reports from Konjic, and it says the fighting started in Konjic as well: "Our villages of Obri and Vrci have been attacked." Tell us, please, whether those villages are closer to your area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And were those villages indeed attacked on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at the following page, where it says that combat operations are continuing and that in Doljani, "one of our soldiers were killed," and that another soldier is still alive. Now, did you know about the fact that fighting had begun in Doljani at that time? If not, it's not important.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, my knowledge about the events in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Battalion, which was in Jablanica, and everything that happened in the area, I learnt about that in 1994, in April, when I left the encirclement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Alaburic, your last questions give the impression that there was an attack and then the attackers killed a soldier. If you read the whole passage, it continues saying: "He wounded himself while under the influence of alcohol, and he died later." So it's a bit difficult to connect this to any kind of military attack, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, but there's another wounded soldier that is mentioned, and my question was about the fighting in the Doljani area, because as events unfolded, we will see that there was fighting towards Doljani, and that particular village will be specifically mentioned, so we'll see that there really was combat going on there. But, yes, I agree with what you've said. I take that on board, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, on Doljani, the witness said that he only heard about that in 1994. I don't know whether it's useful for you to continue asking questions about this, because what he knows about Doljani relates to 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he learnt about what happened at the relevant time in 1994, so the witness's answer can be relevant for these proceedings. And my second comment is that I did not ask the question after the witness's answer because Judge Trechsel rightly intervened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So let's clear this up, Mr. Juric. Can you tell us what it was that you learnt in 1994, about Doljani, about April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left the encirclement at the end of March 1994, I happened to meet some of my co-fighters, and we talked about what had happened in the Jablanica area during that time. And from this person or this group that I met, I learnt that they had been attacked on the 14th as well, just as we had been in Konjic and the other ones in Klisa, and that there was heavy fighting, and he told me that a large portion of civilians, and several fighters with them, managed to escape from the siege, but that quite a number of people had been killed, but those who didn't succeed in pulling out were transferred to the museum in Jablanica. So that's my information about that event.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on now. And in the area which relates to Prozor, the report from Prozor, in paragraph 4 we see the following. It says: "Today the commander of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade asked for reinforcements from the Rama Brigade, from a launcher on the villages mentioned, and he stated that they were in a dreadful situation, and "you should start immediately before it's too late." He says: "The Rama Brigade fired 107-millimetre launchers, one charge on Kruscica." And then it goes on to say: "We have forbidden our artillery fire before an order to fire is received and before the commanders are appointed who will be in charge of the areas of responsibility and before observation posts and wire links are established, so as to be able to follow the shots -- observe the shots and corrective reports properly given. There were requests today for open artillery fire, too, which we did not permit for the reasons mentioned above." Now, my question to you, Mr. Juric, is as follows: Did you know that the commander of your brigade, that is to say, the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, asked for reinforcement and assistance from the neighbouring Prozor brigade of Rama and particularly with respect to artillery support?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now let's look at the report from Konjic once again, and that is on page 4 of the document, sir, Mr. Juric. I don't know where this is in the English text, but it could be the penultimate page. Anyway, the report from Konjic for the 15th of April, 1993, and it says the following: "During the night, large movements of Muslim forces were noticed. There are movements of a sabotage group from the village of Mrakovo and Rodici, Jablanica municipality, in the direction of the Didik [phoen], a very important hill of Boksevica." Now, tell me, Mr. Juric, this hill of Boksevica, that was the strategic feature mentioned earlier on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, on page 5 it says that large movements were noted from the village of Celina towards the village of Grevici, which is located in the Prozor municipality to the north of Boksevica, and everything is geared towards taking Boksevica, and if that happens "then we will be in a situation from which we cannot emerge." Now, tell me, your knowledge of the situation there and the terrain, tell us whether the BH Army managed to take control of Boksevica, or had it been able to take control of Boksevica, would the HVO in that area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Ms. Alaburic. Please go more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise to everybody. I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to what you know about the situation on the ground and according to what you know about the ground, would you say that if Boksevica had been taken by the BH Army, the HVO in the territory of the three municipalities, Prozor, Jablanica and Konjic, would indeed have been put in a hopeless situation, as it says in the report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boksevica is indeed strategically the most important feature, especially in the area of responsibility in Klis. Whoever is in charge of Boksevica is in charge of the road towards Jablanica, Prozor, and it also controls the entire territory of Klis, all the way up to Obri and Vrci and where they border on the municipality or the city of Konjic. In my opinion, at that point it was the most decisive feature and whoever held this feature held the control.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we look at 2D246 now. It's an order issued by Commander Enes Kovacevic. In item 3, he says where one battalion is supposed to go and be prepared for offensive on the positions of the HVO. What I'm interested in is the following, I quote: "Upon the complete mobilisation, the 2nd Company is to take positions in Boksevica and be prepared for offensive operations." This document is dated 14 April 1993. Would such an order on taking Boksevica correspond to what was going on on the ground and what we have just discussed, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Under item 5, can we now look at where it says: "Upon the complete mobilisation, the 4th Battalion, with its 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Platoon, should take positions in the direction of Risovac, and the 5th Platoon has to go in the direction of Doljani and be prepared to carry out decisive defence until the moment the assistance arrives. The positions on Obri should be reinforced by anti-armour equipment and one platoon control the traffic there, and as soon as the combat starts, you should not allow passage in the direction of the villages of Sovici and Doljani." The date on the document is 14 April 1993. Would you say that this order corresponds to what you know about the movement on certain units of the BiH Army and the objectives and targets of their actions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said briefly what I know about what was happening in the area, so I wouldn't be able to provide you any more details about this. I've never seen this before. I've never met this before.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document, which is 4D453, 453. It has already been admitted into evidence. That's why we will not dwell upon it for any longer time here. The commander of your brigade is Zdravko Sagolj. On the 15th of April, 1993, sent a request for assistance to the Main Staff, to the operations zone of Zeljko Siljeg, to the operation zone of South-east Herzegovina, to the HVO of Central Bosnia, to the Rama Brigade in Prozor. He also says that Konjic has come under attack by the forces that had arrived from Bradina and Igman. According to what you know, for the purpose of that attack, did other forces of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina arrive in the territory of Konjic at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Already yesterday, I said that we were attacked by the forces that came from elsewhere. Zuka's units, Black Swans, Swallows, and some special MUP units from Adzic and so on and so forth, it was those units that carried out the attack, rather than the units that were in town.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the last sentence, it says: "Start moving while we are still alive." One could conclude that the situation was indeed alarming, and if the HVO did not receive a substantive assistance in a short period of time, it would lose all the relevant positions in the territory of Konjic municipality. Would you draw the same conclusion, based on the last sentence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now we are going to skip a few documents, Mr. Juric, because we don't have enough time. We're going to skip two documents, and we're going to dwell upon the next one, which is 3D557. This is a handwritten order issued by Arif Pasalic on 16th of April, 1993. It says here -- or, rather, Arif Pasalic says that the forces of the HVO in the Neretvica sector are in a dire position because they don't have enough manpower. Would that be a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat? I am finding it difficult to read the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: He says that the HVO is in dire straits because they don't have enough manpower. My question is this -- is whether this was indeed correct.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next sentence, Arif Pasalic says that the HVO forces requested from their artillery in Pisovac [phoen] to pound the positions of the BiH Army north of Neretvica. We have just mentioned those requests for assistance in artillery. Can we then conclude that this statement on the part of Arif Pasalic is also correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In item 3 of this document, it says: "HVO units are expecting assistance in manpower from the areas in the north, and the HVO units in Kiseljak have been ordered to come to their assistance across Bradina." Would you say that this expectation of assistance in manpower in Prozor is a correct statement on the part of Arif Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's now look at what it says in the order itself. Arif Pasalic says or orders all the forces not to allow the arrival of new forces from Prozor towards -- across the villages of Kacuni, Grevici and Bradina. Did you know that the BH Army prevented the arrival of assistance in manpower in the territory of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I'm aware of that. In all those places, all of those places were encircled by the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's skip two more documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, the interpreters are beseeching you to go more slowly, beseeching you. The problem stems from the fact that when you're reading a document which has already been translated into English, the interpreters have no problem translating from your language into French -- into English, but since the French interpreters do not have the text, they are handicapped by this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to take the opportunity to ask for a clarification. Mr. Juric, you were presented with this letter, where Pasalic thinks that the HVO is expecting support from Prozor, and previously we have seen that Prozor was asked to bring in reinforcement, and you were asked whether the statement of Pasalic that the HVO was expecting assistance in manpower was a correct statement. Your answer was: "No." Could you explain what this "no" means? What was wrong? In which way was Arif Pasalic wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In military terms, commander Arif Pasalic looked at the situation on the ground and he thought they were controlling the area, so it was impossible for HVO units to penetrate through those areas and come to the assistance of those who were encircled. I know only too well that Zuka's units were on Bradina. They held the plateau there, and they launched attacks on the villages of Obri and Ivice [as interpreted], so from the direction of Bradina, nothing could penetrate towards Klis. And the area between Klis and Prozor was also covered by the BH Army, so there was no way for the HVO to help the units that were encircled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Juric, but one can still expect something. I mean, one asks for assistance. It may not be possible to bring the assistance, but one may still have some hope. So it's not a real contrast to say they're expecting help, if it is in fact not possible to bring the help. That's what I wanted to clarify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, just an additional question. If I understood you correctly, in Konjic you expected assistance from Prozor, but you expected artillery support, not manpower, because people could physically not cross the territory and reach you because that territory was under the control of BiH Army. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll skip the next two documents and we'll move on to 4D599. You are familiar with the document because it was prepared by Bruno Stojic's Defence as their own document, and that's why I believe that we will go through it really quickly. This is a combat report by Esad Ramic to the commander of the 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and let's just look at the most important features. The report is for 17 of April, and it says that feature Stari Grad is encircled. Tell me, please --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. What's the document number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 599, 4D599. What is the document that you have in front of you? Maybe I can assist you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be a mistake, Ms. Alaburic. 4D599 that we have is a report of the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. My assistant tells me that the document, I don't know why, has not been included, but I would like to address the honourable Trial Chamber to look at the document in the binder that has been prepared by my learned friend Nozica. At the moment, unfortunately, I don't have the number of the document, so I would kindly ask my learned friend to advise me in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D1305. 2D1305 is the number, and in the future that's the number that I will be mentioning, and that's how we are going to ask for its admission. You have it in the electronic court. This is a combat report by an army [as interpreted] from the BH Army. It says that the HVO is encircled in Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Juric, would that correspond to what you knew about what was going on on the day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next feature that is mentioned is Zlatar. It says that that feature is also fully encircled, that it has been encircled by 60 soldiers from the Black Swans unit, 40 members of the special units of the Hadzici MUP, and 80 soldiers of the 7th Brigade from Konjic. It is also said that so far around 20 HVO soldiers have been captured. Mr. Juric, would this description of the event correspond to what you know was going on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everything's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the HVO positions in Polje Bijela. It says that the BH Army forces have disarmed 15 soldiers. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is where there were defence lines facing the Army of Republika Srpska, and this is where the positions were manned by the HVO and by the BiH Army, and that's how the HVO soldiers were disarmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Go to the next page, please. You will be able to see it on the screen, sir. The next page refers to the village of Radesine. It says that the village is encircled by the forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct, was that the case, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And now let's look at the end of the paragraph, and then I'll ask for your comment. It says, and I quote: "We will attempt to bring the job to an end in Konjic as soon as possible, and then, together with all the brigades, we're going to launch a counter-attack in two different directions. The first one will be Konjic-Jablanica-Mostar, and the second will be Konjic-Prozor-Rama." Mr. Juric, could you please comment on this part of the report? What is this part of the report actually about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already spoken about this in my testimony. What this gentleman is reporting about to his superior clearly points to the fact that the top echelons of the BiH Army had planned an action to clean Konjic as soon as possible and that BiH Army units could proceed further down towards Mostar and Jablanica. They were supposed to clean the HVO in Konjic because they were the only HVO units that stood in their way towards Jablanica and Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, I can conclude from what you have just said that Konjic was a very important strategic position for the beginning of the offensive on the part of the BiH Army. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the area of Konjic, in the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to the defence plans of the JNA, held a special position and had a particular significance in the defence of the former state?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the books from which I studied, a lot of actions -- a lot of offensives did go through Konjic and started in Konjic. For example, the battle on the River Neretva was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And when it comes to the area of Konjic, did the government of the former Yugoslavia have special shelters there where the government of Belgrade should have withdrawn in the case of war? Were there special depots built there, depots of ammunition and weapons, was there a significant war industry located there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The area of Konjic and Igman as well, did it have some significance if one wanted to prepare an action to liberate Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific? I don't know what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Sarajevo was encircled by the Serb forces. If the BiH Army had wanted to organise and implement an action to lift the blockade of Sarajevo, would that area of Konjic and Igman have been significant for the implementation of such a plan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were talks about that, the military area or the military features, which were prepared in case of an aggression against the former Yugoslavia, that command would have been in that area. In the same way, the BiH Army planned to use the area from which to organise actions, operations, and implement their plans, by the same token.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your explanation. Now let's look at the following document, which is 4D445. This is another combat report by the BiH Army for 18 April. Feature Zlatar is mentioned here, and it says that the BiH Army had taken that feature. Does that correspond to what you know; Zlatar had fallen in the arms of the BiH Army? Was that the fact?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Events in the town and in the neighbouring villages are described. What I am interested in is the penultimate paragraph, where it says: "It remains to liberate the strongholds on the left bank of the Neretva river, Turije, Zabrdje, Pomol, and Ljubinje." Turije, Zabrdje, Pomol, and Ljubinje. Tell me, please, this is the area where you were; is that correct, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, Pomol is not on the left bank but, rather, on the right bank. The gentleman who issued that report did not know exactly where Pomol was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says: "The operation will take place tomorrow." And now I'm interested in this next sentence, and I quote: "The objective is to free as soon as possible and help Jablanica." And then it goes on to say: "And further." Now, could you tell us what it means, "help Jablanica further"? Does it mean to take control of all the territory in Konjic, to move towards Konjic, and then Mostar, et cetera; is that what it means?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where the units are being included into the two axes or directions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the last sentence, it says: "According to your dispatch for negotiations with the Chetniks of the 23rd of April, 1993, at Butmir, Mr. Handzo, Mustafa, has been assigned, who is a graduated political science expert." Now, did you know that the BH Army, at the same time with attacks on the HVO, was negotiating with the Chetniks or, rather, the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was talk of that, but I can't say either way. But rumours were going around that there was some kind of negotiations or talks going on, but I can't really say anything about that because I don't know about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's look at the next document, which is 4D1565. And this is once again a report from the BH Army from the 18th [Realtime transcript read in error "14th"] of April, 1993, and I'm interested in the last portion of that report, where it says: "Last night at 1800 hours, we sent a unit composed of 70 men to carry out an attack in coordination with the Rebici village unit, from a direction on Radesine, in order to assist the Ljubinje Battalion in Celebici and to clear up the Konjic-Ostrozac road. We sent a part of our forces to Boksevica and a part towards the village of Doljani." Now, tell us, please, Boksevica and the village of Doljani, they are the geographical locations that we mentioned earlier on; isn't that right, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, this description of events, does it correspond to what you know about the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The village of Radesine was under a total siege and encirclement, and from this report we can see that it was held by the units in the encirclement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. I'd just like to correct a figure in the transcript. On page 21, line 2, the date of this document was erroneously recorded. So it's not the 14th of April, 1993, but the 18th of April. Now, I'm probably running out of time, but I'd like to show Their Honours the ethnic structure of Konjic. I'd like to deal with that, so I'm going to skip over all the other documents that I prepared and ask to have pulled up on e-court document 3D1070, 1070, page 5 of that document, which relates to Konjic, and which I don't have in my set of documents. So from this document, we can see -- well, the text is in Croatian, so we'll help the Trial Chamber out there. It says that the total number of inhabitants in 1991 was almost 44.000; that the number of inhabitants in the municipal centre, that is to say, in the town of Konjic itself, was 13.729. And then we have the total number of members of various ethnic groups, and then we have "Others" or miscellaneous. And if we scroll down, we'll be able to see precisely what you told us and described to us, Mr. Juric; that is to say, that most of those villages were either Muslim or Croatian, and there were some Serb villages as well. Now, I would just like to ask you for your comments. Looking at this map, one could say that the Croatian villages were concentrated in two particular areas; to the left of Konjic in Zabrdje, Zaslivlje, and Turije, Zabrdje, Zaslivlje and Turije, and we mentioned those earlier on; and then the second large concentration of Croatian villages is in the upper left corner, which is the Klisa area; right, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now, if we have a little more time, let's look at the geographical maps that I have prepared for your testimony here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have time to look at all three maps, Your Honour? I'd like to be able to show the witness all three maps. If not, then I'll just show him the last map. But may I have your guidance on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's move on so we don't waste time with the last map. The last document in my binder is 4D1219. It's that map that I'd like you to look at now, 1219, which shows the situation in the Mostar, Jablanica and Konjic area in mid-September 1993, the last document in my set. And from this document, we can see that the entire area in Konjic municipality was under the control of the BH Army, with the exception of the small blue enclave around the village of Zaslivlje, Zabrdje and Turije. Tell us, please, Mr. Juric, this description of the situation, does it correspond to what you know about the events on the ground?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely that area, the area that we defended and defended successfully.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at the document just before that, 4D1216. If I've used up my time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica [as interpreted], please hurry, because your time is almost up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's just see how the situation developed. So we'll move backwards. 4D1216 is the map I'd like us to look at. It's the same area, shows the same area, and it's the situation to the end of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And if we just look at the Konjic area, we'll be able to see that this entire area was under BH Army control, but that except for the enclave that we mentioned a moment ago in those -- the three villages, there was another enclave under the control of the HVO in the area of Klisa. So does that correspond to what you know of the situation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely that enclave. It is Obri and Vrci, which fell last. The soldiers surrendered, and they were captured and taken to the camp in the sports hall, and that was at the beginning -- and at the beginning of July, by the 5th of July, they had taken control of the line and this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. And now the last document that we're going to take a look at, the previous one, 4D626, and this is a map of the Konjic area and the situation on the 24th of April, 1993. And underlined we have the names of the Croatian villages which were taken control of by the BH Army. The arrow indicates places which were currently under attack on that day by the BH Army, and the circle indicates the Croatian enclave or pocket near Konjic, around the three villages that we mentioned previously. From this map, it would follow, Mr. Juric, and I apologise if I'm not going to read the names of the villages correctly, that up until that day, that is to say, the 24th of April, numerous Croatian villages fell; for example, Trusina, Puscak, Orliste, Budisina Ravan, and not to enumerate all the other villages that are underlined in blue. Take a look at the map, please, Mr. Juric. I'm sure you'll understand it and find your way around, and tell us whether the map corresponds to your knowledge of the situation and events on the ground in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Juric, thank you for your answers. Your Honours, thank you. That completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. Witness, I have only one follow-up question for you. I could have put the question to you earlier, but I wanted to wait for Ms. Alaburic to finish. You've told us that the ABiH took Konjic to go towards Jablanica because strategically this was an important thing, it was important that the ABiH take Konjic and then only go to Jablanica, with the idea of going on Mostar. It's a military theory, of course, which is perfectly plausible. But when we look at the map - unfortunately, we don't have the map right here - but there is a route, Jablanica-Bugojno, if you go towards the north, and so the ABiH could have gone through Bugojno and Mostar and to leave Konjic aside, to bypass Konjic. Because you were in a pocket, you were encircled by the ABiH, and in Konjic there were also elements of the 7th Brigade of Konjic, from my point of view it was maybe not necessary to take Konjic, but from the knowledge that you had of the terrain, please tell us if the ABiH could have taken the Bugojno-Jablanica-Mostar road without attacking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as the area that you mentioned is concerned, Jablanica, Bugojno, and all the other names, Vakuf, et cetera, I really don't know about that area, nor could I talk about that and those axes, because I don't have the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you for your answer. We'll get back to that with other witnesses. Madam Prosecutor, you have the floor, and you have two hours for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to the Trial Chamber, to everyone in and around the courtroom. If possible, the Prosecution would like a short break. We've had some computer problems, our case manager has had some computer problems, and we would to also like distribute the Prosecution exhibits. So if the Trial Chamber doesn't mind, we would appreciate a short break before starting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, not a problem at all. Let's take a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are back. We have our binders, and you have the floor, Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Juric. My name is Hedvig Moe, and I am an attorney with the Prosecution. And I will ask you some questions, and some of them will be related to the documents that you now have in the binder in front of you. And I will direct you, in the same fashion as the Defence counsels, to the documents that I will ask you questions about. First of all, just a few introductory questions about Konjic municipality. It's correct, isn't it, that Prozor, that's the neighbouring municipality to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And Gornji Vakuf is also a neighbouring municipality to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little further, not quite neighbouring, a little further off. Konjic municipality does not border on Vakuf, it's not neighbouring to Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I would like you then to go to the first document. It's in the binder, and it's numbered P00154. P0015 --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, but what was the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: P00154. Have you found it, Mr. Juric? It's the second document in the binder, and you'll first have the English version of the document and then the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And before I go into the document itself, a piece of information that was kindly given to me by Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic. In B/C/S, the document has only one page. In the English translation, there is some additional information on page 2 that is not part of the B/C/S original. So we'll be working with one page only, the first page in the English version, which corresponds to the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, if you look at the bottom of the document, you can see that it's signed by Mate Boban, and up in the left-hand corner you see that it's dated the 10th of April, 1992. It's an order that goes to all municipal headquarters of the Croatian Defence Council. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I would still like to ask you about the contents of the documents, and I'll read from the first paragraph. It says "Order," that's the headline, and it says the following: "Since the start of the aggression on the Croatian territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there has been inconsistency in the use of the name for the Croatian forces in Herceg-Bosna. The former TO, serving the Serbo-Chetnik armada, does not exist for Croats in Herceg-Bosna. Therefore, during its meeting of 8th of April, 1992, the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna reached the decision that the supreme body of Croatian defence in Herceg-Bosna will be named the Croatian Defence Council." I'll skip the paragraph and keep reading: "The Croatian people were abandoned, but they organised and defended themselves. They created their own defence and formed their own defence forces. The Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna has decided that the Croatian Defence Council will have exclusive supreme command of these forces. This body is the only legal one and its name is the only official one." And then the last paragraph: "All other military formations on the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna are either illegal or enemy formations. All other titles are no longer in official use." So what Boban is saying in this document is that the HVO is the only legal defence force in Herceg-Bosna. Were you aware of that at this time in April 1992, that this was his view?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that this is the first time that I see this document and the first time that I read through it. And it says at the top here that it was self-organisation on the part of the units, and I explained the situation in our area of Konjic, how it happened there. I said also that the HVO in Konjic was established at the beginning of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: My question was to the HVO in Herceg-Bosna, as a whole, and the fact that Boban, on behalf of the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, Boban says here that the HVO is the only legal defence force in Herceg-Bosna. Did you know that that was the HVO view -- the central HVO view at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've already said that I can just address military matters. Now, anything directly linked to politics, I really don't have enough knowledge to be able to talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. Juric, this seems to me to go to military matters. It refers to the HVO as a defence force, and I'm asking you whether you knew that Mr. Boban and the central HVO considered the HVO only to be the legal defence force -- the legal force in Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question in any precise terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: So does that mean that you never -- you didn't hear about that from -- that that was the central HVO view at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object. First, it's been asked and answered. Second of all, based on his answer, it would appear for him to do anything other than speculate at this point in time, I don't see how he has the knowledge to answer that question, as phrased. And now she's turning his answer into a question, which I believe is unfair, because she's trying to make the gentleman appear as if he's either uncooperative or the question assumes facts which are not in evidence, in which case if he doesn't answer, then the question would appear to be giving an answer to which this gentleman cannot ascribe to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Moe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: A different document, Mr. Juric. That would be P00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Witness, that's all very well, I understand what you are saying. You said that the HVO was formed in Konjic in June 1992. This document is dated the 10th of April, so it's quite possible that this document was something you were not aware of. However, in Konjic, were you never made aware of a document of this kind? Because a while ago you told us that this was the first time you saw this document. In the media, nobody said anything about the fact that the HVO was the only armed force in 1992, in the month of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in April 1992, there was the Territorial Defence in Konjic municipality, manned jointly by the Croats and Muslims, and I said that very clearly, that we acted together, worked jointly, cooperated until June 1992. That was 16 years ago, so I can't remember these documents now or discuss them, therefore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Moe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Let's move on to a different document, Mr. Juric, and this is P00195. This is, as you can see in the upper left-hand corner, this is dated 8th of May, 1992. It's the HVO General Staff, and it's signed by General Ante Roso. And it says -- well, I'll ask you first: Have you seen this document before, Witness?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I still would like to ask you about the contents of the document, and this is a military document, to put it that way, in the sense that it's from the General Staff. And it says: "On the basis of until-now-reached agreements, and in the case of need, I issue command ..." In the territory of the HZ-HB, the only legal military units are the units of the HVO. And that would be the same item of the same order/command that we just saw in the Boban order. So, Mr. Juric, this is May 1992, and you said earlier that you joined the HVO brigade in Konjic in September 1992, so let's go to September 1992. When you joined the HVO in September 1992, you were made aware that your superiors, the General Staff's view, was that the HVO was the only legal military force in Herceg-Bosna, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not with that position, that somebody informed me that the HVO was the sole legal force in Bosnia-Herzegovina, not in those terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: In what terms, then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were two active forces, the BH Army units and the HVO units. Those were the legal forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Well, it says here that the only legal force are the units of the HVO. That's the General Staff view. So who told you the opposite?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just talking about what I knew, and what I saw, and what was going on in my town, in the place I was in, and that is Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: So you're saying that you were never made aware of the General Staff view, as set out here in the Roso command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll take that on board and I'll move to another document. It's P00200. P00200 is an order from Tihomir Blaskic, and it's dated 11th of May, 1992, as we can see in the left-hand upper corner. And it says: "On the basis of the orders received from the Main Headquarters Confidential number 01-331/92 of 8th of May, 1992 ..." And I'd like to stop there for a second, because if we go back to P00195, that's the document we just looked at, we can see that up in the left-hand corner there is a number that complies with what I just quoted from the Blaskic order. The number is, again, 01-331/92. So Mr. Blaskic is referring to the rules of order when he makes his order. That's his foundation, and Blaskic says, item number 1: "The only legal military units in the area of Kiseljak municipality are HVO units." So, again, the language is that the only legal military units or force is the HVO. So this is Blaskic giving an order in Kiseljak municipality, and I put it to you: Wasn't the same type of order made in Konjic municipality? Weren't you, at your municipal level, told that the only legal military units are HVO units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I never saw Mr. Blaskic. I just heard that he was the commander, but throughout the war I never saw him. And what happened in Kiseljak municipality, well, I know nothing about that, nor could I have any knowledge about that. Now, the question that I'm being asked now, that this order came down to us, I really know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: That was not my question, Mr. Juric. My question was, and I'm quoting: "Wasn't the same type of order made in Konjic municipality? Weren't you, at your municipal level, told that the only legal military units are HVO units?"

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period when this order was issued, at that point in time I was a fighter, a combatant in the units, the joint units of the BH Army and HVO, because we were still acting jointly. So I was there as a fighter, not as a commander or someone close to the commander, for me to be acquainted with this order. And the system of information at that point in time wasn't functioning at all for me to be able to have any knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Let's go to September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't wish to interrupt or to object before the witness gave his answer. I allowed the witness to answer so as not to be accused of helping him out. But can we go back to the previous question asked by my learned friend? It has two questions within it. The first question is asking the witness to make conclusions, whether he can make conclusions about whether Blaskic's order was applied in Konjic. That's the first part of the question, and the second part is whether that was the situation in his municipality, that is to say, Konjic municipality. And the witness has already answered. Now, my point is this: This is a witness to fact. He hasn't been called in here to make any conclusions. He is a witness dealing with the facts. He can say what he knows about, heard, possibly saw, and so on, but not about Boban's orders in Kiseljak, did this happen in Jablanica, and so on and so forth. He can't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kovacic, the witness is a military man. At the time, he told us that he was serving in the Territorial Defence. Perhaps the HVO municipality [as interpreted] in Konjic may have told them at the time, We have received a document from Mate Boban that states this and that. And he has said that he had not heard about this. Ms. Moe, the questions you put to him, well, that's all very well, but it would have been much easier to conduct your investigation, given the number of investigators you have, to look into the archives in Konjic and check out Blaskic's order, and you could have checked this out in the municipality of Konjic and we would not have wasted any time. The witness, at any rate, is not aware of any of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Witness, to go to document P10926, please, 10926. That will probably be towards the end of the binder. 10926, please. 10926, that's an order again. It's from the president of the Croatian Defence Council, Mate Boban, and it's dated 10th of June, 1992, and it says: "Pursuant to the Statutory Decision on the provisional establishment of the executive authority and administration on the territory of the HZ-HB of May 1992, I hereby order: The establishment of the executive authority of the HVO in the Konjic municipality, pursuant to Article 7 --"

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my learned friend. As far as I can see, the witness has not been able to locate the document. While you're reading, I can see him going through the binder, and maybe the usher could help the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, please, could you go and help the witness. I think he's a little bit lost. Even the Judges are lost at times, all the more so a witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Otherwise, Witness, you can just look at the screen. The document is displayed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Again, Witness, this is from Mate Boban, and it's an order to establish the executive authority of the HVO in the Konjic municipality from June 1992. And an executive authority of the HVO in Konjic was established on Boban's orders, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in early June. There was a meeting. Actually, my unit was established, Mr. Ivica Zinovic [phoen] and Dinko Zebic came and conveyed to us the order to establish the civilian authorities in the city of Konjic, and this gentleman, Ivan Zinovic [phoen] was appointed. Before that, he was [indiscernible] Pavic's [phoen] assistant in the Main Staff, and Dinko Zebic, as from then on, took over the position as his commander of the HVO military units, and I already said that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move to P10919, please. That would be in front of that document you just looked at. P10919, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Usher, could you sort out the microphones of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: This is from the Konjic Municipality War Presidency, and if you look at the end of the document, it's signed by coordinator of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army and the War Presidency of the Konjic Municipality, Zejnil Delalic. The document should be on the screen in front of you also , Witness, and it says: "Public announcement. Regarding the announcement of the Konjic HVO of 5th of July, 1992, filed under 02-944/92, we are making the following announcement: "The Konjic HVO has surfaced as a self-proclaimed organisation allegedly in charge of supplying a complete range of products from Croatia." And I'll skip four paragraphs: "The HVO, together with certain reactionary MUP forces or, rather, former members of the State Security, is trying to carry out a coup and overthrow all legal institutions of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Witness, you said that the executive authority of the HVO had been established in Konjic, and I put it to you that on a local level also in Konjic, the Konjic HVO was trying to overthrow the legal institutions of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Konjic. Isn't that right, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, let me go back to what I've already said, and that concerns the politics, and let me just put it simply. What I can read here is ridiculous. I find it ridiculous because I know that during that period of time the gentleman that worked in the Political Department of the HVO did not follow such guide-lines, nor did they want to achieve what I can read in here. As far as I know, because I was not part of this, I am not aware of any political decisions of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll go to another document, then, Mr. Juric, and this will be P10918, please. P10918 should be right in front of the one you just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Could we have the assistance of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: This is later. This is dated, up in the left-hand corner, 8th of March, 1993, and it goes to the War Presidency of Konjic Municipality. And we see that it's signed by Peric, and it has the stamp of the HDZ, Konjic Municipal Board. And the subject is: "Response to your letter dated 4th of February, 1993." "In respect to your letter," and there is a reference number and again the date, "concerning the functioning of the War Presidency and Executive Council in the Konjic Municipality ..." And I'll go to the paragraph that starts a little above the middle of the page: "The authorities in BH are not legitimate because they have discredited themselves with their passivity, ineffectiveness. In compliance with the policy of the HDZ of BH, the HDZ of Konjic Municipality has set up, at the municipal level, the transitional executive authorities and administration in the form of the HVO/Croatian Defence Council. The HVO of Konjic Municipality functions as an integral part of the HVO HZ-HB." So I put it to you, Witness, that the HVO, as established in Konjic municipality, was a parallel authority that functioned in addition to the legitimate BH authorities. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not denying that those authorities existed and were active. However, I cannot agree that they were independent in what they did. Everything was done in agreement. And I emphasise that you are actually talking about politics, and I don't know anything about these things. Dragutin Peric was the president of the Croatian authorities in Konjic. Please, if you can reduce your questions to the military matters. When it comes to the politics, could you please not ask me anything about that, because I almost don't know anything about that. I was interested in politics in as much I needed to know just not to be a complete ignorant in that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Well, the two last documents I put to you, Witness, the foundation for my question was that you were in Konjic at the time, and you also referred to the meeting where the HVO, the executive authority, was established in Konjic in June 1992. So I put it to you that based on the fact that you were there, you must have known these things, that there was a parallel HVO authority that was set up in addition to legal BiH civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did say that a meeting was indeed held. However, I did not say that I was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Well, I'll move on to military matters related concretely to you, Mr. Juric, and I'll ask you to go to document P01637, please. P01637, please. P01637, in the English translation, it says date illegible, up in the left-hand corner, 1993, but in your B/C/S original, Witness, it says "9th of March, 1993," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And we see that this is a command on the assignment to Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Konjic, and it says that Dragan Juric, born 10th of July, 19 -- sorry, 1955, is appointed deputy commander, and it's sent to the OZ Command, the unit, and the Personnel Administration, and it's signed by Bruno Stojic. And there is a stamp, and in the English version it refers to the stamp being the Military Police Administration, but again Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic informed me that there was no reference to the Military Police Administration, it's the Department of Defence, which complies with Bruno Stojic signing it. So, Witness, you were appointed deputy commander by this document, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you. We're still in March 1993, and I'd like you to go to a document that you looked at with Ms. Nozica yesterday. And it's number 2D00253, and it's in the binder that you have in front of you. 2D00253. That's a document that was shown to you yesterday. It's of 20th of March, 1993. It's a memo from an ABiH meeting. And you said you didn't know about a meeting yesterday, but nevertheless, you spoke about the contents when Ms. Nozica asked you some questions, and I will do the same. This is going back to what the Presiding Judge Antonetti brought up with you yesterday, and I'm trying to -- I'm going to ask some follow-up questions to that, and I'll take you to the second -- or the first paragraph after the subject, and this is an assessment of the military and security situation, and I'll go to the last sentence of that paragraph. And it says: "This deterioration," that would be the deterioration in the relationship between the HVO and the state authorities of the BiH. "This deterioration is caused by the HVO's enforcement of a parallel authority." And I'm not going to go into that again, but I'll ask you the following: It says here that examples of HVO enforcement of a parallel authority are: Enforcement of a taxation system. And there was enforcement of a taxation system on behalf of the HVO, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's skip two items, and I'll ask you here: "All motor vehicles," still on the same page, Witness. "All the motor vehicles are provided with new license plates of the so-called Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and flags are raised on buildings not authorised to display national insignia." It's true, isn't it, that motor vehicles were provided with new license plates of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm moving to page 2 of this memo. It's page 2 both in the English and the B/C/S version. It's the second paragraph. It says: "In view of the above," that is, the list of items considered by the ABiH to be enforcement of parallel authority, in view of this "or the Ruling by the Constitutional Court of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the cancellation of all the regulations covering the establishment of the so-called Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna (Official Gazette of the RBiH number 16/92), dated 18th of September, 1992 ..." And my question goes to what I just read here, Mr. Juric. There was a reference here in the memo to a ruling by the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina that cancelled all the Herceg-Bosna regulations. Were you familiar with that Constitutional Court decision basically rendering Herceg-Bosna illegal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: You never heard about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on that question, perhaps the witness could be asked: Did the state government -- the Muslim government, I should say, because it was the Izetbegovic government, did it publicise that throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, because now if you're going to pose that question, then the next question should be -- or there should be some sort of a factual predicate which actually it was widely disseminated, assuming that the Constitutional Court was in fact properly constituted, which we maintain it was not, it was no longer a properly-functioning court, it was an Izetbegovic court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you are pleading and making witness statements now, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And I think it's for Ms. Moe to decide what questions she wants to put to the witness. The witness said he didn't know about the decision of the Constitutional Court, so how would he know about whether it was made widely public?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's the whole point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: That is asked and answered, implicitly, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let me cover this problem differently. In 1992, in Konjic, did you have radio or television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Were you able to listen to Radio Sarajevo or Television Sarajevo? Were you able to hear those two and watch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So my question is going to be very difficult. If you asked me the same question, I would not be able to answer it, because we are talking about facts that took place 16 years ago. But let me put this question, nevertheless: At the time, do you remember hearing radio announcers or TV speakers saying, Our Constitutional Court just cancelled all decisions of the HVO? Do you know if you heard that on radio or on television in those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if my memory serves me correctly, already in 1992, in March -- or, rather, in April of that year, we had lost all the TV channels. I remember that vaguely at the moment. I can't give you the exact date, but in any case, it was in the first half of 1992 when we no longer had any TV reception, so we have to exclude the possibility of anybody of us watching television. And as for radio programmes, I never followed those anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Still in the same document, Mr. Juric, I'll ask you to look at item 7. It's numbered 7, and as we know, this is a 20th of March ABiH meeting, and it says: "The line of defence against the aggressor shall be fortified ..." And the aggressor in this sense, that's the Serbs, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should have been the Serbs. However, there's a comma which means a lot here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Well, when the ABiH makes reference to the aggressor, that's the VRS, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, could you read the sentence to the end? Maybe then I will be able to tell you something about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you more generally. The aggressor, that's the VRS, isn't it, and not necessarily related to this document, but in general, the ABiH at this time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Army of Republika Srpska was the aggressor. However, Jablanica, Kute, Here, and Scipe are mentioned here as the direction, connected the Army of BiH with the neighbouring villages. I'm confused. Maybe the HVO is meant as the aggressor, because at that meeting we were no longer considered the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. Juric, and this is a document -- the next document is P01866. 01866. This is a record of the Operational Zone South-Eastern Herzegovina, a commanders meeting with the commanders of the immediately-subordinated units, and assistant commanders, and it's dated 13th of April, 1993. You were present here, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking you directly is that it says here -- well, the second paragraph: "Absent from the meeting were the commander of the 1st HVO Knez Domagoj Brigade, the commander of the Konjic Herceg Stjepan Brigade, and the commander of the Tank Battalion." So it says that your commander wasn't present. It also said, in the introduction, that it was a meeting for assistant commanders, and as we established previously, at this time you were assistant commander of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade. Doesn't that indicate that you were present, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not an assistant. I was a deputy. The brigade commander had six of his assistants for intelligence, for security, for logistics, for establishment and personnel, and an assistant for IPD. I was a deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: So you're saying you weren't present, but I'll ask you about the contents of the document and see if these are issues that you were told about subsequent to the meeting. It says --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. The question hasn't been put, so I would like to intervene. If it says in the record that he was not a commander, and the witness says that it wasn't him, I don't know what would be the basis for a further question, and how could the witness have heard anything about the minutes? I believe that the witness is expected to speculate from now on. The question hasn't been put. That's why I've intervened. Otherwise, I wouldn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. It's been a long time since I've been on my feet, but I'm going to intervene in this situation, with apologies to my good colleague. Your Honour, this is an absurd objection. We've heard over the last two days, last day and a half, repeated questions to this effect, asking the witness to speculate about all sorts of things where he was not physically present. Indeed, virtually the entire Petkovic so-called cross-examination, which in the Prosecution's continuing view wasn't cross-examination at all, it was simply a friendly examination, was one speculative question after another about things where the witness was not presently there, but he was only too happy -- the witness was only too happy to give answer after answer after answer to the leading questions put by the Defence counsel. So for this objection to be raised now is completely inconsistent with the last day and a half of practice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go on, Madam Prosecutor. You may continue on this topic. The witness will maybe remember something. Maybe he'll tell you that he was not present at the meeting at all, but you may put your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. My questions go to the witness's knowledge of the contents of the document. That's what I would like to ask him about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And it says here, that's the end of the paragraph that I was reading from, just above item 1: "... the following conclusions were reached ..." And number 1: "The BH Army has succeeded in carrying out most of the plans from record number strictly confidential 16-8/08-62/93 of 20th of March, 1993 ..." And I'll stop there for a second, because if we go back to 2D00253, which is the document we just looked at, that document, the ABiH memo, has this same reference number, 16-8/08-62/93. So this meeting of the operational zone commanders and assistant commanders, including your unit, refers to this memo. In other words, the HVO was in possession of the ABiH memo from the 20th of March, 1993, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Mostar? As far as I can see, the meeting was in Mostar. That's where it was held.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, Mr. Juric. As I said, this is a meeting of the operational zone, and there's a reference to the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, the commander not being present. Let me put it this way: You, your brigade, had knowledge of this 20th of March ABiH memo, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only the operative zone could have had knowledge of that, but as my commander wasn't present at the meeting, then most probably he couldn't have been informed and have knowledge of what is said here, with all the details and the elements from the meeting held on the 20th of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: But given that this was -- presumably this was important information, wouldn't your brigade be informed about it from your superiors, the operational zone?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this question is -- this question is directly asking for speculation. It should be rephrased. He might be asked whether anything like that was later received by the brigade, but not, Wouldn't it be possible, blah-blah. It is speculation, pure and simple.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Moe, please move on and go straight to the point, because I really have trouble understanding what is it you want to highlight.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Let me ask you more precisely, Witness. It says here, right above the item number 1, that reports from the Konjic and Jablanica areas were read out. Therefore, it seems that at this meeting, reports from the Konjic and Jablanica areas were received. Then my question is: Didn't this information of the 20th of March memo go in the other direction, that is, from the operational zone to the Konjic HVO?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
