utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I apologise again for intervening. There's communications coming from the accused in the Croatian language that the witness can presumably hear. It's completely inappropriate. The Chamber should put a stop to it immediately, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, let me just remind you of one thing, and that is that during my cross-examination, we read reports from Konjic for the 13th of April, 1993, and so therefore the reports mentioned here, which my learned friend has just referred to, is precisely what we saw a moment ago. So I think that will help in understanding the issue better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Witness. We're wasting a lot of time on this question, but there is something that's still bothering me. Mr. Lasic, who is the commander of this zone, he organises a meeting, and at the meeting various reports are raised, reports from the Konjic area, for instance. I would like to know how is it that your commander, or his assistant, were not present at the meeting? Is there an explanation for this or not? I can understand that you were not there. I believe you, that you were not there. I can understand that. Militarily speaking, I cannot understand it when it's the commander of the operational zone who organised this meeting. So shouldn't he have called commanders of his operational zones? Maybe the commander is there, maybe he's ill, or at least his assistant? But you're telling us, No, we were not there. In fact, your commander, was he there or was he not there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, he wasn't present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, he wasn't there, fine, because he was absent. And you weren't there either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who drafted the report on the situation in Konjic then? Had there been any written reports prior to that? In that case, Lasic, Miljenko, said, We have received a report. Could things have happened this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd just like to clarify a point, with your permission. The commander at this time spent, in the village of Kostajnica, in Klisa, as we've already said, spent time, and the 13th and 14th was when the all-out offensive was launched against the HVO in Konjic. Now, where the commander was, the brigade commander was, he had packet communications, so that the IPD assistant who at that time, and I remember this vaguely, it is possible that he was with him there and that he sent out this report, but I can't say that with any certainty. It's just something I seem to vaguely remember when I go back to these events in my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Moe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm moving on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, you've talked extensively about what happened in the Konjic-Jablanica area in late March and April 1993, and you've talked about Muslim or ABiH acts, and I put it to you: Isn't it true that what the Muslims did at the time was, in fact, provoked by the Croats, by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just speaking about Konjic. I didn't mention Jablanica at all, because I have no knowledge about Jablanica, about that period, March and April, and for as long as I was under an encirclement.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but we had an intervention there from the interpreter that the first part of the witness's answer wasn't recorded, just the second part relating to Konjic. But before that, he said that he is quite certain that the HVO in Konjic did not attack the BH Army, and he's 100 per cent certain of that. That's what he said, 100 per cent, the HVO did not attack the BH Army. And that wasn't recorded, but the witness can repeat his answer, because we see the interpreter's intervention on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, do you agree with the fact that you said, with 100 per cent certainty, that there had been no attack on Konjic against the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HVO did not attack the BH Army. That is 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Moe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Well, firstly, Witness, I clearly remember that you'd been talking about what happened in the Jablanica area when you were questioned by Ms. Alaburic and Ms. Nozica. Isn't that correct? And this goes to March and April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. If my learned friend said that I asked him about Jablanica, she can refer to the transcript, because I didn't ask a single question linked to Jablanica. So she can check the transcript to see where that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Well, let's go with Ms. Alaburic, then. You did talk about Jablanica, didn't you, Witness, when you were questioned by Ms. Alaburic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd just like to remind you that Doljani were mentioned, and the witness said he didn't know what had happened in the village of Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll move on, that is, I will go back to my original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: -- question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: My question was not what you answered. My question was: I put it to you, isn't it true that what the Muslims were doing in March/April 1993, let's say in the Konjic area, that that was provoked by the Croats, by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state once again, and let me repeat that, that the HVO from Konjic, that wasn't provoked. I don't know what Croats you're referring to, but the Croats from the HVO in Konjic did not provoke that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to a document. That's P01798, please. Yeah, I apologise, it's a loose exhibit. Thank you, Judge Trechsel. This is the minutes of the 34th session of the HVO. It's held on the 3rd of April, 1993. As to participants, we can see that Jadranko Prlic, Mate Boban and Bruno Stojic were present, among others. And I assume you haven't seen this document before, Witness, but I would still ask you some question to the contents of the document. It says that the agenda of the meeting is: "Discussion of the documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan." And if we go to page 2 of the document, the penultimate paragraph, it says that: "Until the Republic is fully demilitarised, the armed forces will be organised in accordance with the relevant documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, and in the accordance with the joint statement issued after the agreement of Mr. Mate Boban and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, who led the delegations of Croats and Muslims at the peace talks. The statement was signed by Mr. Mate Boban, and its integral text reads as follows:" And then I'll go to -- I'll skip some paragraphs and I'll go to page 3. And at page 3, the last paragraph, it says: "At this meeting, the HVO HZ-HB adopted the position that if the aforementioned statement is not signed by the leaders of the Muslim delegations in provinces numbers 3, 8 and 10, then the basic premises in the peace plan, which states that all ethnic armed forces have to withdraw to their domicile provinces, should apply." And then continued from there on page 4: "If the joint statement is not implemented, the appropriate military and other authorities of the HVO HZ-HB shall implement this provision of the basic document of the peace plan in regions numbers 3, 8 and 10." You knew about this, Witness, didn't you, that the HVO decided to unilaterally implement the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, including in Konjic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, you said straight away, and that is correct, that I didn't know about this meeting at all. And as for the Vance-Owen Plan, I saw it in the papers. It appeared in the press. But as to its details and all the rest of it, I really can't say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Moe, I'm a little bit surprised. You know that the Bench controls the cross-examination of witnesses, and you see whether a witness is able to answer a question or not. The Vance-Owen Plan question is a question which has been addressed many a time by prominent people, Mr. Okun, ambassadors, and so on and so forth, and all these questions have been raised already, and you're putting these questions again in the presence of someone who told us he knows nothing about political issues and he knows nothing about the Vance-Owen Plan, which he read about in the press, so you're wasting your time. We are wasting our time, and you are wasting your time. So you may reflect on this, and you may proceed, since you have two hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll try to take it down to the municipal level, and the witness was in Konjic at this time, in one of the municipalities involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: So I'd like to go to page 5 of this same document, please. And the first paragraph here in the English version, it says: "It was also agreed at the meeting that in the next couple of days, members of the HVO HZ-HB should visit all municipalities in the provinces numbers 3, 8 and 10 in order to explain to the authorities the essence of the Vance-Owen documents and the conclusions of this meeting." So I put it to you, Witness, that Konjic was one of these municipalities, and members of the HVO HZ-HB were to visit the municipalities to inform on the conclusions of the meeting. You were informed of these conclusions, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to laugh because I'm confronted with all these difficulties. I don't know about this. I know that through the Vance-Owen Plan, there was Konjic somewhere in there. What number, I don't know. And looking at this, well, I find myself in dire straits. Who received this, where this was discussed, I really can't say. I have absolutely nothing to do with any of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Okay, excuse me. I'll move on to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, irrespective of the question that has been put to you, as far as you remember, no one came from elsewhere to your municipality to discuss or to talk to the people and say, well, there is this plan and this is what is going to happen? People weren't gathered to discuss this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's not what I'm saying, 100 per cent. I don't say 100 per cent that nobody came, but I wasn't aware of that, nor do I know about it, but I'm not claiming that nobody came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, do you think that the second -- you were assistant commander of the brigade, so you were a high-ranking military. You were the second man in the command. Is it possible that you were not made aware of the fact that a prominent figure from the HVO was coming to this town to spread the good news?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was a reserve captain first class in the former JNA and I'm familiar with the military hierarchy and the military matters. From the military aspect, a commander had to be present at all the meetings, and his assistants for the IPD, and they are the ones to inform us about the situation. And since that unit was established in the war and the situation was as it was, it was far -- or far removed from all things military or things as perceived in military terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Maybe I can just add a question. Mr. Juric, it seems that your attitude was -- or what you tell us now is that as a military high officer, almost commander, next to the commander, politics were none of your business. Is that what you are -- what your attitude was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that politicians run politics and commanders run a military. In military circles, there were people who were designated to deal with politics, and they were assistants for information and political activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Moe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Following on from that, Mr. Juric, I put it to you that you were much more involved and had much more knowledge of both political and military issues of the HVO and the HZ-HB than you are now telling us, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll go into some documents on this. Can we please go to P10927, P10927. P10927, if you look at the end of the document, it says that it's from Brigade Deputy Commander Dragan Juric. And if you go to the upper left-hand corner of the document, you see that it's dated the 20th of May, 1993. And that would be when you were in the area of the three villages that you mentioned, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And it says -- well, it says, on the right-hand side, that it goes to the Main Staff, Mostar. It goes to the Operational Zone Command in Tomislavgrad and the Rama Brigade Command, to Zeljko Siljeg in person, Prozor, and it says "Report from Konjic": "During the day, we received two reports and were asked to forward them to you." Where were these reports from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This does not feature my signature. It says "Deputy commander of the brigade." Anybody could have put that, and this is not a valid document. Second of all, from the area where I was, not even a bird could carry a document of this sort, so I did not go on reading the complete article that has been written. If I managed to read it, then I will possibly be able to tell you something more about it. However, my opinion is that this was sent from the office of the brigade commander in Klis, which had a package communication and he could send it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Maybe I can be of assistance. Maybe the witness could be shown the heading of the document, which shows where the document was sent from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it says "Kostajnica." That's where the commander was. As I've already told you, he had a package communication system, and through that this could be sent. From the area where I was, I could not -- at that moment, I could not communicate with anybody. I did not have any elements that would allow me to send something of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: But if we look at the document, Mr. Juric, and that would be the original B/C/S version, it does have your name below the text, and it does have a stamp that says that it was received at the Main Staff -- the General Staff. And this would be packet communication, wouldn't it? That's why there is no signature underneath? Can I have an answer, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: This was packet communication, wasn't it? That's why there is no signature underneath?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Are you challenging the authenticity of this document? Are you saying that it's not from you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not write this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: But your name is underneath it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name's there, but I did not write the document, nor could I have. You see where the document was written. It says so in the heading "Kostajnica, 25th of March, 1993, at 2200 hours."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I do believe it should be the 20th of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, one moment, please. I assume that in the Stjepan Herceg Brigade, there were people that were drafting text, intellectuals or law students. You were on the front-line. You had your weapon and your feet in the mud, so I'm sure you had other things to do. Since this is packet communication that comes from Kostajnica, does this mean that there's an officer in charge, or a soldier who is able to read and write, who would have drafted this on the basis of documents and after having listened to the radio, and then he prepares his report of a political nature and sends it on to the authorities, and he puts your name, since you were the second in command? He could have also written in there the name of the commander. It so happens that you were the second in command and that your name is there; is that why you tell us today that you did not prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is correct that I did not draft the document, and it is also correct that in the village of Kostajnica, where the brigade commander was, that his assistant for IPD was also there with him. And judging by the wording of the document, I can only assume that this was drafted by the assistant for information and political activities in the brigade, in the brigade, who was together with the commander in Kostajnica, where the packet communication system was, and that was the one that was used to send the document to the operations zone and to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be of assistance. The witness has said it. Can you ask him where he was physically at the time? He did say that in his examination-in-chief. He said that physically he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A while ago, I said you had your feet in the mud. Where were you, exactly? How far from Kostajnica were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Almost 30 kilometres away. That's the distance between Konjic and Kostajnica, 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In which town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Turije --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Turije.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Zabrdje, Zaslivlje, that's the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, I would like to say just one sentence that might help better understanding. If you remember the map that I showed the witness, we saw two enclaves. One enclave was Kostajnica, and the other one was Turije village, and the witness says that he was there. So the witness was never in the place where the document was issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Moe, we will have a break now, a 20-minute break, since it is time to have a break and think about all this. The witness was not there. He was 30 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Please replace that there had been an attack on Konjic against the HVO by that there had been an attack on Konjic by the HVO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resumed. With respect to the time left, you still have 54 minutes. I hope that there won't be any objection, unless Ms. Nozica has additional questions, but I hope that we'll be able to finish the testimony of this witness today. Ms. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I have one more question to the document that we looked at before the break, Mr. Juric. That's P10927, which you talked about, and this question goes to the contents of the document. And I read out to you a while ago from the start of the document. During the day, you received two reports and were asked to forward them to you, and then there are quotation marks, and the next paragraph should go to the contents of that first report, and I'll read it out: "Today, the Chief of Staff of the so-called ABiH, Sefer Halilovic, broadcast the public threat over Muslim Radio Sarajevo to the HVO of Konjic and the HVO of Jablanica, and all the Croatian people in Konjic and Jablanica. As he said, unless the HVO stops with persecutions in Mostar, it will cease to exist in Konjic and Jablanica. Since the HVO in these areas is only defending the survival of the Croatian people, who are threatened by an invasion of Islamic fundamentalism, the intentions of the military junta from Sarajevo are clear. What is involved is actually ethnic cleansing of the non-Muslim population from areas that belong to the Croats under the Vance-Owen Plan." And I put it to you, Witness, that the Vance-Owen Plan and the areas that belong to the Croats, these were issues that were discussed amongst you, weren't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the Vance-Owen Plan, in military terms, we did not ascribe it a lot of significance. We did not consider that issue at our briefings. We never debated that. It was a political issue, and there are others who discussed this. And as for what you have just read out, I did not write this. Even if I had, I would not have put the so-called BiH Army and some other things, because the BiH Army was also a regular army, as the HVO was, at least for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. Juric. Can you please go to document P10911, P10911. This is a document -- an order that's dated 20th of May, 1993, and we see that it's signed by you, Herceg Stjepan Brigade Deputy Commander Dragan Juric, and it's sent to, we can see from the left-hand side lower corner, Republika Srpska Army Command and Ljubinje commander, and it says: "On the basis of earlier talks between representatives of the Republika Srpska Army and the Herceg Stjepan Brigade Command, I issue this order: "1. All the contacts between the mentioned subjects shall be realised by persons authorised for that purpose by the superior commands. "2. The brigade's deputy commander, the 2nd Battalion commander, and the commander of the Ljubinje post, are the sole persons at the post authorised to plan and coordinate the joint operations and activities being planned in that regard." And, Mr. Juric, these plans regarding coordination of joint operations and activities, I put it to you that those were joint plans by the HVO and the VRS to fight the Muslims. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never worked together against the BiH Army, not for a single moment. We were not engaged in any military operations together with the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: But this goes to the joint -- these refer -- this document refers to joint operations, and it goes to the Republika Srpska Command. Are you saying these are not references to joint VRS and HVO operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plateau that is referred to in this document, the Ljubinje Mountain Plateau, before the conflict between us and BiH Army, the Republika Srpska had its positions there. It says here that with regard to any conversations and agreements, only the person mentioned herein can maintain contacts with Republika Srpska in that area. There were some other persons who appeared and wanted to do things that we were not aware of, and that's why this order had been issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Based on your answer, that the HVO never worked together against the BiH Army with the VRS, I'd like you to go to P02910. P02910, that's a document from Siljeg, and it's dated the 22nd of June, 1993, and it goes to the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Kostajnica. It should be on your screen as well, Witness. It's a short document. It's from Siljeg. It's dated 27th -- sorry, 22nd of June, 1993, and it goes to the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Kostajnica, and it says: "Immediately request XY to open fire on Konjic and Celebici at 4.30 hours." And XY, that refers to the VRS, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know anything about this intelligence. I don't know. The XY and all those things, I don't know anything about that. If you have any further questions, I'm prepared to answer. This is an order that I was not in a position to receive. I believe that this was sent to the commander of the brigade in Kostajnica, if it was. It was not sent to me. I did not have anything to do with anybody from that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: So you're saying that you don't know what the XY means?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, I'm sure I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: But this goes to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Witness, a very brief question. To go back to the previous document, it is handwritten by yourself. You sent this document to the Republika Srpska. I am a bit baffled. Serbs are your enemies. You sent yourself document to the enemy. Did you receive orders to that effect or was it to your own initiative that you did this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at that moment we were encircled. We were effectively the front-line of the Republika Srpska Army facing the BiH Army. We were the living shield -- human shield, both the civilians and the troops. I could not receive orders from anywhere. I did what I could in order to save the civilian population that was in the area, i.e., to protect all the others who were in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Going back to the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. I would still like to go back to that order, the previous one which you have signed, and I still have not understood what the joint operations refer to. What kind of joint operations do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were individuals there who insisted on joint operations, and I emphasised that the joint operations could not be carried out before this was approved by either myself or the commander of the position in Ljubinje. There had been attempts for people to influence the whole situation and to have joint operations carried out, unbeknownst to me, in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, that is quite interesting, perhaps. It doesn't answer my question. You speak about joint operations. What do you have in mind? Not other people speaking about this or that. You have in mind joint operations, and only very limited persons, including yourself, are authorised to negotiate these joint operations. What operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Through the Serb side, we transported civilians from the area in six convoys, and that was our cooperation with the Serbian Army. In that area, there were 300 nationals of Serb origin that we had been looking after at the gravest of moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, I cannot check on the original language. It's not something that an English speaker would think of when he hears about joint operations, but I see I must leave it at that. Ms. Moe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Going back to the document referring to XY, Mr. Juric, P02910, it's going to be on the screen in a short while. You said you didn't know what the XY referred to, but we see that Siljeg is sending this document to the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Kostajnica, so presumably he expected the commander who received it, or the person who received it in the brigade, to know what XY refers to. But you're saying that you did not know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was not in a position to know whether the commander knew the code or not. He could not inform me about the code. The only communication that we had with the commander in Kostajnica was the small Motorola, which is an open communication line, and you could not use it to convey any military information or converse openly, because anybody could have tapped into any such conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: So you had communication with Kostajnica, then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said that it was the Motorola, the radio sets that were similar to a mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. Juric. Yesterday, you said, when being examined by Ms. Nozica, that Konjic municipality had a Muslim majority before the war of 55 per cent; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 54 or 55 per cent is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And you were asked by Judge Antonetti about the notions of Greater Croatia, in accordance with a document, and you said that Konjic had a Muslim majority and could therefore not be part of Greater Croatia. And I'll quote from the transcript from yesterday. You won't have it, but just listen to what I'm saying, repeating what you stated yesterday. It's page 57, line 16: "Well, this kind of thing couldn't have been discussed in Konjic, because the ratio between Muslims and Croats, in terms of numbers of inhabitants, there were far fewer Croats, perhaps just a third or even less than a third, so the Croats couldn't have accomplished what you've just said, this greater Croatian state or whatever you just said." That's what you stated, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you some maps, and they are in the loose exhibits that should be -- should have been given to you earlier today. Maybe we can have the assistance of the usher. It's, first, P09276, please, and that would be map 9. That's the last map that you have, Mr. Juric, in that little folder. If you have a look at the map, please, you can see that this goes to the ethnic composition of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991, and you can see Konjic here, can't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And it confirms what you said, that that's one of the municipalities with an absolute Muslim majority; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Please go to map 5. That would be the page prior to the one that you're looking at now. I still don't appreciate comments from the accused, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No comments, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: That's a map that shows -- that says the Banovina, 1939, showing BiH municipalities, and we can see that Konjic is part of the Banovina of 1939. So you knew about that, didn't you, the Croatian Banovina and the fact that Konjic was included in the Croatian Banovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm this with any degree of certainty. While I went to school, we did not learn about Banovina in history classes. To be honest, I was never much interested in knowing anything about the boundaries of the state at this time. Now I can see this - I'm looking at the map - I've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: But were you familiar with the fact that Konjic was part of the Croatian Banovina prior to seeing this map right now? You were, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I'm not intervening very willingly, especially in view of your intervention, Your Honour. The witness has already answered and said that he did not know of that before. Let's look at, together, the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In fact, he just said that he was not taught at school about this, and he just told you also that he saw this map for the first time now. But of course you can ask him if he's ever heard of it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Yes, that was my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Before seeing this map here, Mr. Juric, were you familiar with the fact that Konjic was part of the Croatian Banovina?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. Perhaps it would be of assistance to us if we were to ask the witness whether he knows what Banovina Hrvatska or Croatian Banovina, in fact, is and means.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I would like to put the question as I put it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Prior to seeing this map, Witness, were you familiar with Konjic being part of the Croatian Banovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my family, where I lived, and the circle of people that I moved around in, we never discussed these banovinas, nor did I know about them, and especially not whether Konjic [Realtime transcript read in error "Croatia"] was part of the Croatian Banovina or not, because in the period that I lived in, this was not a subject that was discussed at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a different map. This is map --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a correction. Line 23 on the previous page, the witness said whether Konjic was in the Banovina, and it was recorded whether Croatia was in the Banovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, before we go into the maps, because we're going to be spending some time on maps that we already have seen, the gentleman, based on what he's already presented, I don't see how much more value to the Trial Chamber will be to show the maps that are in evidence, that the trial already knows, based on the answers that he's given. I just mention this in order to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's try to save time, Ms. Moe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll move on to map number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: That would be the first map in that little bundle that you have, Mr. Juric.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: This is a map that shows the Croatian Communities of Herceg-Bosna and Bosanska Posavina 1991, and this map shows that Konjic was part of Herceg-Bosna, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question. Now she's testifying. The gentleman has indicated that he doesn't know, first of all, and she's testifying, based on that question. How do we know, from her representations, that this map is actually accurate? That's my whole point of my objection earlier, and I will be doing this on every map, on every question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Moe, you can tell the witness the following: "I'm showing you a map. What can you tell me about this map?", for instance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Well, I'll go back to my starting point. You see that this is a map, right, Witness, and it says that the Croatian Communities of Herceg-Bosna are shown on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, I object. Just because it says it doesn't mean it's so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I do believe I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] I'm going to repeat. Let me just check that interpretation is working. Unfortunately, we see that in 1991, the Herceg-Bosna Croat Community is there. I mean, we have a text, but we can't do anything about it. Ideally, it would have been better not to have the text, but unfortunately the text is there. So this being said, Ms. Moe, please put your question, and I'm waiting for an answer and the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I have the same question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: This map shows that Konjic was part of Herceg-Bosna, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says on the map. According to this map, the map I'm looking at, that's how it's surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And Konjic was part of Herceg-Bosna, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say again, that's what would follow on the basis of this map, but who drew up this map and who conceived it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, I find this a bit difficult. Are you telling us that you do not know whether Konjic, your place, was part of Herceg-Bosna or not? Do you want us to believe that you ignore even this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that judging by this map here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Please answer my question. I am asking you, as a high military officer who worked in Konjic, were you ignorant of the fact that the municipality of Konjic formed part of the Croat Republic of Herceg-Bosna; yes or no? You knew or you did not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I did know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, I wish to point out, based on that form of the question, that you're suggesting that the entire municipality, as opposed to areas within the municipalities, were part of Herceg-Bosna. We took -- we had extensive testimony on that, and I think that's the fallacy with the map. The map draws in the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, that's the Defence's point. I accept that you -- and you have now said that you doubt this, and I think it would be helpful to go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I guess -- well, then if that's the case -- that's my position. I want to know whether it's the Bench's position or your position that the entire municipality of every municipality drawn in this map was Herceg-Bosna, because that's the problem that we have with the map, and others would have. Areas may be part of Herceg-Bosna, but the way it is, and it seems that we're still in the middle of the Defence case, and now based on your question, you have asserted a fact of which I need to be aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, unfortunately, so far the Defence has not shown us evidence of certain parts of Konjic not being included in Herceg-Bosna, and if we see this, of course, we are ready to say that most or a large part, or whatever, of Konjic belonged to Herceg-Bosna. But if you look at the basic text, you have the municipality of Konjic mentioned there. I did not use the term "territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, and I appreciate that. I would, however, point out that we did present testimony concerning maybe not every single municipality, but, for instance, we had testimony where we did debate this issue or tried to counter the Prosecution's theory of this issue of territory versus areas. That was my point, Your Honour, and that's why. But if the Court feels it is necessary for the Defence to bring in a map which shows exactly which areas within which municipalities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think this is meandering a bit far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has clearly answered that he knew that Konjic was part of Herceg-Bosna, full stop, and we're not going into the details of "podrucje" or "teritorija." I leave that open, I expressly leave that open.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that. You did press the witness, Your Honour, you did form an opinion, you told us that, I realise that, and now I'm fully aware that we need to present further evidence on this point, and I appreciate that. I'm not trying to meander. I apologise for taking the time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honours, but in view of the question just raised by Judge Trechsel, I have to intervene. On page 71, lines 5 and 6, Judge Trechsel told the witness the following: "Do you want us to believe that you ignore even this?" And I consider that that position on the part of Judge Trechsel is not commensurate to this stage of the proceedings. Judge Trechsel presented his view here; namely, that the witness didn't know certain things, and now he says: "Do you want us to believe that you ignore even this?" I think that that is a conclusion that the Prosecutor may be allowed to make in his closing arguments, based on the statements by this witness; but I, as Defence counsel for Mr. Bruno Stojic, I have to say that an assessment and evaluation of this witness's testimony will be weighed up in the way he testified. He testified about things he knew. He was very frank in saying what he knew of and what he did not know about, and he told the Defence that and he told the Prosecutors that. So this gives rise to concern, seeing this sentence on the record, because it seems to be a position taken with regard to this witness's testimony before the witness has concluded his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. So the record is balanced, this trial, as the President mentioned several days ago -- yesterday, excuse me, this trial has been going on for three years. The Chamber has heard an abundance of evidence on this point. This map is in evidence. Other documents are in evidence, which clearly show absolutely, without question, clearly show -- and this is argument, but that's what counsel are doing now, so I'm doing the same thing -- show that Konjic was part of Herceg-Bosna. It's been in document and document after document, map after map after map. We cannot -- no party, including the Defence or the Prosecution, can put three years' worth of evidence to every witness. There comes a time when everyone in the courtroom must presume to build on a certain foundation, and there's nothing improper whatsoever, in my submission, and again I want the record to be balanced -- excuse me, maybe Mr. Praljak can sit down until I'm finished. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, please let the Prosecutor finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Judge Trechsel's comment, and again I'm saying this so that the record is balanced. Judge Trechsel's comment was entirely proper in keeping with observations on the state of the evidence, which a Judge can do at any time in these proceedings, and it's simply we're really wasting time. And I wouldn't have gotten on my feet, except that at this point, given the comments that have been made, I think that the record had to be balanced. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To avoid wasting any time, let me say this. To know whether Konjic is or is not part of the Croatian Community, it's important to establish a distinction between the notions of de jure and de facto. There is one document, which is P79, which has not been mentioned, which is the Constitution of Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which includes Konjic, so de jure, according to this document, Konjic is part of the Croatian Community. Now, de facto, perhaps this was not the case, so the Bench, at the end of the proceedings, will have to assess whether this document P79 is an illustration of what actually happened and reflects what occurred. Nonetheless, I'm still keeping my eye on the time, and I shall give you the floor back now, Ms. Moe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll move to my last map, and that would be P10068. And that's also one of the loose documents, Witness, and that's map 37. I think you're in the wrong -- in the wrong bundle, Mr. Juric.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could we have the assistance -- some assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it on the screen up here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Okay. It's 10068, map 37. And this -- Witness, this map shows the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, 25th of March, 1993, and you can see from the legend that certain numbers, provinces, are to be Muslim areas, certain provinces are to be Serb areas, Croat areas, and mixed. Excuse me. And you see, don't you, that according to this map, Konjic is to be a Croat area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And that is in spite of the fact that, as you said, Konjic had a Muslim majority prior to the war; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: And it would not surprise you, would it, if many of the Muslims in Konjic did not feel so positive about the municipality being part of a Croat province, according to the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a difficult question for me to be able to provide an answer, what the Muslims thought about the Vance-Owen Plan, or Konjic within that plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Let me ask you a different question, then. It would not surprise you, would it, if many of the Muslims in Konjic did not feel so positive about Konjic being part of Herceg-Bosna, would it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Moe, I think this question is perceived as asking for speculation, and I do not quite see what the interest for the Chamber is of what the witness thought in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll move on, Judge Trechsel. I'd like -- I don't appreciate the comments from the counsel, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was talking to my colleague. It was not a comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Can we please go to P10 -- excuse me, P10922. That's in the binder, Witness. This is an article from "Vreme" magazine. 5th of July, 1993, that's the date. "Vreme" magazine, that's a Serb publication, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: From Serbia? From Serbia? I asked you a question, Witness. Is "Vreme" magazine a Serb publication from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that, but I'm reading this now, so -- well, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: On page 2, there is a photo. That's a photo of you, isn't it, to the right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Do you remember making a statement to the journalist from "Vreme"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember just now, but I can explain what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'll ask you the questions, thank you. And I'll go to your statement. This article goes to an alliance between the VRS and the HVO at the time, and I would like to ask you about your statement, as I said, and that would be on the page that is numbered 33 in your article. You can see the page numbers down to the right. It's on page 4 of the English translation, and the headline is "An Orthodox Bishop and a Friar." And the next paragraph, I'll read it out: "The Chief of Staff of Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Mr. Dragan Juric, was somewhat more specific and realistic, revealing a part of a real picture of this alliance. The events here have compelled us to establish cooperation with those whom we have recently still pointed our guns at. It didn't take us long to put that time behind us, and I think that the politicians should realise that this is the only way to defend what is left of our people. Muslims are very strong here. They have brought people from Eastern Bosnia, and there are a lot of mercenaries, Mujahedin, from Iran, Kuwait and Morocco. They obtain their weapons mainly via UNPROFOR pipelines, and we can prove that. Money is always behind everything." And then what I would like you to pay particular attention to: "As for the border of Herceg-Bosna, we have no disputes with Serbs, but neither side can live with Muslims any longer. I think that we shall make a joint effort and force Muslims to leave these areas." And I put it to you, Mr. Juric, what I said to you before the break. I put to you that you had good knowledge, both politically and militarily, about what was going on at the time, and I put it to you that what you say here proves that point, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I cannot assess what the gentleman who wrote this wrote. I was wounded on the 2nd of July and in a very difficult situation, and I was transferred because I had a temperature, I was running a temperature, and they were going to amputate my leg. I was transferred to Republika Srpska and the war hospital there, and I was operated on there. I was running a high fever, and after that I remember that some journalist turned up to interview me. That's all I can say, as far as the condition I was in when this was written, because I stayed in the area for seven days, I had all these troubles to contend with, and their policemen were in front of the door to the room I was lying in and I kept hearing people shout, Let's see that Ustasha commander who's lying in bed there. So after spending eight days there, they sent me back to Turije, and my recuperation lasted another month and 20 days, roughly. So I don't deny that I was there, I don't deny having said some things, but similarly as to what is set out here, I think -- I don't think it's all truthful and I think it has been added on to, because in those days I was having a great deal of problems and my life was hanging in the balance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: That concludes my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one point of clarification, Witness, unless there has been a mistake. You were taken to this hospital for your leg to be amputated. Were you actually amputated or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no, I underwent two surgical procedures and they were able to save my leg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would kindly ask the usher to distribute some documents that I've been able to prepare in the meantime, and I also believe that I will be able to call them up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Mr. Juric, let's start with the moment you were wounded and the last thing you said, and that was that at the time, you were treated in the territory that was held by the Serbs. Did you have an opportunity, you who were in the territory of Turije, Zabrdje and Zaslivlje, as you have described for us and for the Trial Chamber in your direct examination, did you have an opportunity to be treated anywhere else? Did you or any other members of your unit have an opportunity to choose anywhere else to be treated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had two physicians in the area who were working in a garage. There were six beds there, and they could only treat some slight wounds. Everything else, we had to seek approval to transfer such wounded, and the Serbs helped us with that. However, three of our soldiers, two members of the military police and another foot soldier, were taken for treatment and were liquidated up there. They never returned. It was only last year that the body of Mario Vidackovic, a military policeman, was exchanged. And as for the other two, we still don't know what their lot was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, you have just told us that you were forced, if I understood you well, because there was no other place for you to be treated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And that three members of the HVO who went for treatment in the territory of Republika Srpska have been liquidated and never returned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you know that at the moment when you were taken for treatment? Did you know what risk you were exposed to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I am going to repeat and ask you: Did you have any other opportunity? Could you be taken anywhere else to be treated in your condition?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Juric, while you were in the area, first as the commander of the area and then in the staff or in leadership of the area, how many civilians, approximately, or members of the HVO were treated in the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but I would say that their number was up to 20, maybe less than 20. I'm saying up to 20 because I'm not aware of the exact number. If I ever knew it, I've forgotten in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, let me go back to a document that was shown to you by the Prosecutor. It is not in my binder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat the number. 10911.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You don't have to -- I believe it's the document that -- look at it in e-court, Mr. Juric. This will save us some time. It's an order that you signed, and I will kindly ask you to comment upon it. Mr. Juric, you said that there were no joint operations with the Army of Republika Srpska. Kindly tell me whether the Army of Republika Srpska, at the time while you were in the area, acted or was engaged against the position of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were there in that area, the VRS would occasionally shell the town of Konjic and certain positions. It opened fire on our defence lines. Shells fell on our defence lines. We had two seriously wounded who succumbed to his wounds, and we had some other slightly wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In the operations launched by the Army of Republika Srpska against the position of -- positions of the BiH Army when you were also hit, or any time later, had you ever engaged in any negotiations between you, as the commander of the sector, and them to engage in joint operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no negotiations, there were no agreements to that effect. However, when it comes to that area and that conflict in the area, they controlled all that very well because they were much higher above the area, so from all of their positions they could have a clear view of the position and where the combat was taking place. And as soon as a combat started in one of the sectors, they would start acting against that sector in order to protect themselves, because they were aware that if our lines had been broken and if the area was taken control of, that the situation would be compounded and they would come under threat. They kept us there as the human shield, as the first defence line, although they had lines behind ours and there was a minefield between us and them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly when you said that between you and the Army of Republika Srpska, there were minefields? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was the strip of minefields?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It went from Ljubinje, down to Turije, and according to my estimate it was a hardly-accessible area, and in some places the mines were not necessary. In any case, the length of that area was about five kilometres with minefields. It was hardly-accessible terrain. No minefields were necessary there because there were streams and brooks, and very hard to negotiate for a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that in front of you, there was the BiH Army, and that above you, in the pocket where you were, there was the Army of Republika Srpska. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you also said that you negotiated with the Army of Republika Srpska about the transfer of civilians, and there was quite a large number of civilians in your territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We also saw and heard, from the question that my learned friend put to you, and I followed up on it, that you were treated together with some other members of the HVO in that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You also said, and I want to repeat, that there were no joint military operations involving yourselves and the Army of Republika Srpska against the BH Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, in the situation that you found yourselves in in the pocket, completely encircled, did you negotiate with members of the BiH Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber when the negotiations took place, the negotiations to deal with your unfortunate situation? When did they start, actually? Did they start immediately after you came there? Did they continue until your departure from the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The negotiations with the BiH Army started sometime in July.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. And now I will ask you to look at a document. We shall rely on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I call up P6555. Could we please see it in e-court. I have not prepared it in hard copy because I decided to show the document at the last moment, after my -- after the last question put by my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Look at the document. This is a report from the Herceg Stjepan Turije Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In the meantime, I'm going to say that this document was signed by Mr. Mladen Zovko, Kuhar, and this document originated from the Independent Battalion Herceg Stjepan, Turije. It says in the document that in a conversation with Haris Silajdzic on October 19, 1993, on an exchange of prisoners of war, it says: "I was invited to Silajdzic's place for a conversation." This is what Mr. Kuhar says. Who was Mr. Kuhar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was my assistant for security while I was the commander of the area, and on 19 October 1993, when this was drafted, at the time he was the deputy commander of the area or the -- and still he was the assistant commander for security.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: He says here the meeting was attended by Mladen Zovko and Jerko Petkovic, who represented the Herceg Stjepan Independent Battalion. Is there somebody called Jerko?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was Zeljko.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: "... and the commander of the 6th Corps, Mr. Salko Music, and a member of the Supreme Command, Bosiocic, Zagi, represented the Muslim side. Apart from the talks concerning the exchange, the mentioned individuals offered us to surrender our positions to them, and in exchange they would enable the evacuation of soldiers and civilians from our three territories across their territory. "Haris Silajdzic, during the talks, and I talked to personally, provided guarantees regarding possible operation. On the 3rd of November, I met with Fahrudin Fazlic, also known as Braco, and he informed me that he had been authorised by Silajdzic to negotiate with me regarding the issue of our positions. On that occasion, he offered to buy off from us 70 per cent of our small arms, all the heavy weaponry, and the food that has remained, and they were prepared to pay 500.000 Deutschemarks for all that. "I replied that they could possibly get small arms at the demarcation line and the aforementioned individual accepted that." It goes on to say what the topic of the conversation was and how it went on, and I'm going to ask you this: Did you know about these contacts between the Independent Battalion Herceg Stjepan, Turije, or with your area with the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina to negotiate the transport of you and the civilians from the area ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this period of time I performed the duty of the assistant commander for dealing with civilians, in other words, my job is to accept civilians, to look after them, and for the concern for the civilians in the area. And as for these events described herein, we simply mentioned that in a short briefing, but nothing about the money or the sale of weapons. I didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, my general question to you is this: Did you know that starting from July 1993 onwards, that there were contacts and negotiations both with the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in order to deal with your hard position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you very briefly, how long did the conflict between you and the BiH Army last, until when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the beginning of September 1993. That was the last attack that was carried out, and as of that time, the beginning of September, until the month of March 1994, the BiH Army never attacked us. There were no infantry or artillery attacks. During that time, we even embarked on joint work. A commission was set up which provided for electricity for Konjic, because the long-distance lines went to our area, we allowed that. Joint commissions were set up. We toured the area, and towards the end of 1993, on the eve of the new year, our villages got electricity as well as the town of Konjic. We all got electricity. And one more thing that I would like to say. During the negotiations which were carried out with the other -- the one and the other side, which is very important, we could not transport civilians through Jablanica, because civilians had arrived from there in our area. We transported them through the Serbian side. That was our concession to them for having helped their civilians. And as for the combatants, both sides emphasised that no single combatant from the area could leave the area. First of all, they would be disarmed; second of all, they would be taken to a camp, to detention; and, thirdly, their further lot would be decided by higher echelons, which means that nobody in the area was competent to decide what would happen to such combatants later on, if they surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me just ask you briefly. When you say "both sides," the one and the other side, you mean the BH Army and the Army of Republika Srpska already had Croatian detainees in their prisons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH Army did have Croats in the sports hall up to November, there were 400 of our combatants there. And as for the Serbian side which was in contact with us, I don't know whether there were any detainees there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And did you know that there were prisons further afield on the territory of Republika Srpska where Croats had been kept? Did you hear anything about that after the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The policemen who got killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters. You started by saying you're a policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The policeman, Mario Vidackovic, who was killed up there, he had been taken to the camp in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask you briefly to look at a document that you were shown by the Prosecutor. They are in the big binder that you've received. They follow a sequence in which I'm going to be using them. First of all, you were shown a report signed by Zejnil Delalic, and this is a publication without a date, but it follows on the report of HVO Konjic, and it says here that the HVO is doing something of their own will. The number of the document is P101 -- I apologise, P10919. We have it now. Did you find it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In this public announcement, Mr. Delalic writes against the HVO. It seems that the document was issued in July, although it doesn't bear a date, and he is referring to a public announcement by the HVO Konjic. I'm going to show you the next document to establish a link between the two documents. So this first document is from the month of July, and now look at 2D767, which is the following document in the sequence that has already been shown to you. Have you got the second document in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, a reference is made to a coordinator. We have already spoken in this -- about this document and misinformation which was directed against the HVO about the situation in Konjic, and it says in this document that the coordinator was Mr. Zejnil Delalic. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I believe that you're correct. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please look at the following document. Were there any other coordinators? Did anybody introduce themselves to you as coordinator? I'm sorry for insisting. Did you hear of him being such a coordinator?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not be informed about that. I knew that he was the commander of the Tactical Group TG-1 for Igman. However, since I was not well informed about that, I can't say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I won't insist. Let's look at something else. We saw what the coordinator did in both cases, and now look at 2D798. We have already seen the document. I showed it to you earlier. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And we see here that this is an announcement from a joint meeting which took place in October 1992, two or three months after the public announcement by the coordinator, who said that the HVO was the one provoking conflicts. This is an announcement which was signed by the commander of the staff of the BiH Army for Konjic and the commander of the HVO. We carefully read it. Does it arise from this announcement that there were no significant problems in Konjic between the BiH Army and the HVO; on the contrary, that that cooperation was at a high very level?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. I'm showing you the documents because it has been implied by my learned friend, the Prosecutor, that the HVO provoked all the conflicts, and we clearly see and we insist on the fact that the commander of the staff of the BiH Army in Konjic co-signed this announcement. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well, then. I'm now going to ask you to look at document P01866. Mr. Juric, did you find it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is from a meeting that you didn't attend, according to you, and it says very clearly here that not even the commander of your unit was at the meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber when this meeting took place? Was it at 10.00, as it says here? And you were asked whether you were aware of all these positions, and you said you were not, and it was implied that you could have been aware of the meeting that took place on the 20th of March, 1993, and it says here that the minutes of the meeting were discussed on the 13th of April, 1993. And now I'm going to ask you to tell the Trial Chamber what happened that night. We don't know where the meeting took place. It is to be assumed that it was in Mostar. However, I would like you to tell us what happened during the night between the 13th and the 14th of April, 1993, although we have already spoken about that. Could you please repeat what was said and what you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 13th and the 14th of April, 1993, this was the beginning of an all-out attack of the BiH Army against Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, before that attack, around the 10th to the 13th, did you know anything about the blocking of the roads leading to Mostar that had been carried out by the HVO and a blockade of the roads around Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I apologise. Did you know that the BiH Army, and I misspoke, I apologise, that the BiH Army, around those days, on the eve of that attack, carried out a blockade of the roads around Konjic, especially those leading to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the check-points that were in the area were manned by the BiH Army. There were neither the MUP or the HVO in any of the check-points.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Are you saying that the check-points that had been established earlier, did I understand you properly, on that day were exclusively under the control of the BiH Army and the HVO? I'm going to ask you, and if you don't know, please don't answer. Is it possible that the commander of your brigade could go to Mostar to this meeting and go through all these check-points?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that was the very reason why he didn't go. The answer may not be correct. This is just my opinion. That's what I'm guessing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What is your opinion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that he may have been prevented by the fact that he might have been imprisoned when attempting to pass through the check-points.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now let's look at the last document. I believe that it begs clarification. The number is P10927. Did you find it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, you said that you did not sign this document. I would kindly ask you to provide another very concise explanation. This is a document that obviously originates from Kostajnica. Can you tell the Trial Chamber, when you said, I could not have sent this because I wasn't there, could you tell the Trial Chamber and explain to the Trial Chamber where you were on the 20th of May, since when you were there, and where was Kostajnica from which the document was obviously sent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period of time, well, when this was written, I was in the area between Turije, Zabrdje and Zaslivlje. Kostajnica is at the very entrance into Buturovic field, some 20-plus kilometres away from Konjic, i.e., from the area where I was between Turije, Zabrdje and Zaslivlje.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You already said this, but please repeat. Who was in Kostajnica at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, as for the Brigade Command, there was the brigade commander and his assistant for IPD, i.e., Information and Political Activity. The two of them were in the communications centre, as it were, where the packet communication system was all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, please, just for the transcript, since when were you in the territory of Turije, Zabrdje and Zaslivlje, and until when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there from the 18th of April, 1993, until, and I can't really be precise, it was either the 15th or the 16th of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell the honourable Trial Chamber whether you could in any way send a courier, maybe, on the 20th of May, 1993, and dispatch this report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said to the Trial Chamber there was no way for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, this report is from Konjic. This is not a report from Turije, Zabrdje or Zaslivlje; is that what you could agree with? Look at the first page, please. It says: "A report from Konjic," does it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In this report, it says that somebody was listening to the radio on the 12th of April and the 23rd of April, and there is an emphasis on the letter date, and you said to the Trial Chamber that you were without electricity at the time. Were you in a position to listen to the Radio Konjic on the 23rd of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. In the area where I was, I couldn't listen to the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is what I wanted to ask you. Thank you very much. And further on, although he you have already directly answered this, Mr. Juric, did you have any packet communication in that area? Because we can see in the document that it was dispatched by packet communication on the 20th of May, or, rather, received by the Main Staff on the 20th of May at 2400 hours. Did you have any possibility to send a document from Turije, Zabrdje and Zaslivlje by packet communication?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Juric. I have no further questions for you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much, Witness, for coming to testify at the request of Mr. Stojic's Defence. I would like to wish you a safe return home, and I would like to ask Mr. Usher to escort you outside of this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's hear what's planned for next week. As you all know, Mr. Praljak's Defence will intervene. The Chamber rendered a decision under Article 84 -- Rule 84 of the Rules. Mr. Kovacic will have one hour and thirty minutes to present his -- to submit his motion, and after that Mr. Praljak will be sworn in and he will make his opening statement under Rule 84 bis of the Rules. The Trial Chamber stated that Mr. Praljak will have one hour and thirty minutes. This was handed down. It's registered, and the decision will be translated if it has not been translated yet. So this is something I wanted to tell you already now. We are going to reconvene Monday. We will then start with the 84 and 84 bis procedure, which should bring us to the end of the day of Monday, since one hour and 30 minutes plus one hour and 30 minutes equals three hours, so we will end the hearing on that day.
