Then on Tuesday, Mr. Praljak will be sworn in. Actually, he will not be sworn in again, since he would have already been sworn in on Monday. And then he will, on Tuesday, answer to questions put by his attorney, Mr. Kovacic. So now everybody knows what's going on. Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to say that we understood the French original yesterday very well, and I have just been advised that the English translation has reached us. We may have not been clear in the notification that we sent to you. There will be no opening statement pursuant to Article 84, and it arises from our notification that we plan for Mr. Praljak to talk for three hours, in keeping with 84 bis or 84, depending on the Trial Chamber. But now that we have read the text in the English language, it seems that you have explicitly decided that, so it seems that if I have any additional requests, you will tell me that it is res judicata. I'm saying this for organisational reasons. We would be very happy if Mr. Praljak could talk for three hours. However, if your decision is what it is, I am obviously not going to dwell upon that. General Praljak would then start on Monday, within the temporal limitations that you have provided us with. The Defence would not have any opening statements, because what Mr. Praljak is going to say is defence, and then we would proceed with examination-in-chief. This is our plan, and we hope that nothing unforeseen will happen with that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Since I only have a few more seconds: The last witness for the Stojic Defence will be able to -- will come as soon as it's possible. You will let me know ahead of time so that we know, while Mr. Praljak is testifying, that we may insert this other witness. You've asked for one hour for that witness, so you'll have one hour for you and one hour for the Prosecutor, and then it will be done in such a way that there's no interference.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, I would kindly thank you for giving me this opportunity. We will make sure that Mr. Praljak's testimony is not interrupted. We will make sure to organise the arrival of this witness after his testimony and still in consultation with the Defence of Mr. Praljak. It is my duty to tell you that I have not been in a position to receive medical documentation for the witness whose name I don't want to mention. As soon as I have any information and medical documentation, I will inform both the Trial Chamber and my learned friend, the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I may take just one second. It is still on your decision which we just discussed. We earlier were told that we would start on 4th May, which is Monday. A decision, and probably it is the error, still is mentioning 6 May. But that was not your intention, to change the days? We are starting on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Monday is the 4th of May, it's not the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we're starting on Monday. Very well. Just a few seconds, because I really don't want the Popovic Trial Chamber to be mad at me. So you have a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No, just out of an abundance of caution, and history has shown that sometimes it's better to err on the side of absolute clarity, I take it from Ms. Nozica's comment that the witness that she's referring, based on saying that he will not be called prior to the end of the Praljak testimony, that means he would not be called any earlier than the second half of July. That's how I understand that, then. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I thought too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is for practical reasons. It would be pointless to interrupt the examination of Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I wish you a good day, and the hearing will reconvene on Monday at 1415.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
